---
title: "Install and run Spinorama"
date: 2026-08-22
abstract: >
  Install the Spinorama development environment, metadata manager, command-line
  tools, and documentation dependencies.
---

This project has two audiences: people who want to run the analysis tools and
people who want to develop or contribute data. The setup script creates the
complete environment. The Python environment can also be installed separately.

## Requirements

| Tool | Version | Required for |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.12 (setup scripts) | Python tools and metadata manager |
| Git | Any recent version | Source checkout and contributions |
| Node.js/npm | LTS | Website build and JavaScript tests |
| Rust/cargo | Current stable | Generators, metadata validation, and API |
| Quarto | Current | Documentation build |

## Complete setup

### Linux and macOS

Clone the repository and run the setup script from its root:

```{.shell}
git clone https://github.com/spinorama-org/spinorama.git
cd spinorama
make setup
```

`make install` installs only dependencies: Python packages in `.venv`, a minimal
Rust toolchain through user-local rustup, and JavaScript packages from the lockfile.
`make setup` also prepares website assets and builds the Rust generators and API.
Neither command installs system packages or runs linting. Install Python 3.12,
Node.js/npm, Git, and a C compiler/linker beforehand. Set `SPINORAMA_PYTHON` to
select a Python executable. Existing `CARGO_HOME` and `RUSTUP_HOME` are respected;
the defaults are `~/.cargo` and `~/.rustup`.

Use `make install-dev` for Python test and lint tools, rustfmt, and Clippy. Use
`make python-reference` for optional Python extensions. Selenium browser tests
need `python -m pip install -e '.[browser]'` in the activated environment.
Run `make python-reference` before `make test-python` for the full Python
reference suite; native Rust tests do not need Python extensions.

Activate the environment in every new Bash or Zsh session:

```{.shell}
source env.sh
```

### Windows

Install [Python 3.12](https://www.python.org/downloads/),
[Node.js](https://nodejs.org/), [Git](https://git-scm.com/), and MSVC Build Tools, then run:

```powershell
.\scripts\setup.ps1
```

Activate the environment and set the import path in each PowerShell session:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
$env:PYTHONPATH = "$PWD\src;$PWD\src\website"
```

The setup script installs user-local rustup and enables UTF-8 mode for the current
PowerShell session. Pass `-InstallOnly` to skip assets and native compilation.

## Python environment

To install the Python environment separately from the system tools, run:

```{.shell}
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
export PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PWD/src:$PWD/src/website:$PWD/scripts"
```

`requirements.txt` includes the Python runtime and metadata editor dependencies.
Development, browser, and reference tools are opt-in extras in `pyproject.toml`.
To activate the installed environment without downloading anything, source:

```{.shell}
source env.sh
```

The script also works when sourced through its absolute path from another directory.
It reuses the current SSH agent and leaves your working directory unchanged.

## Run the applications

Open the Python GPUI metadata manager with:

```{.shell}
make metaedit
```

Use `make metaedit SPEAKER="Brand Model"` to open an existing speaker directly.
See [Add speaker metadata](03_metadata.qmd) for TOML editing and validation.

Compute graphs and preference scores from a directory of measurements with:

```{.shell}
python -m pip install -e '.[reference]'
python scripts/compute_spin.py /path/to/measurement-data
```

The command auto-detects supported formats and writes PNG graphs and a
`*_scores.json` file. See [Compute a spinorama](08_compute_spin.qmd) for the
format layout and options.

## Run tests and checks

From the repository root, with the virtual environment active:

```{.shell}
PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests
npx vitest
make check-meta
```

Run the deployed-site checks with Chromium:

```{.shell}
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
make test-dev
```

`make test-dev` runs Vitest against `https://dev.spinorama.org`. It checks
JavaScript asset loading, pagination across up to five available pages, and search.
The checks select a speaker from the live catalogue and accept changes to speaker
names, counts, and ordering between runs. HTTP errors,
failed requests, and browser JavaScript errors fail the suite. Failed tests save
screenshots under `output/playwright/dev/`.

To check a local server or another deployment, set the site URL:

```{.shell}
SPINORAMA_TEST_URL=http://localhost:8888 npm run test:dev
```

In GitHub Actions, run the `Spinorama Javascript` workflow manually to include
the `dev-smoke` job. Set `base_url` to choose a deployment.

Useful formatting and lint checks are:

```{.shell}
ruff format .
ruff check src tests
npx prettier --check src/website
```

Run `./scripts/check_html.sh` when checking generated HTML. The complete
project setup and CI may run additional checks for native extensions and
generated assets.

## Update headphone pages

Run the headphone pipeline from the repository root:

```{.shell}
./update_headphones.sh dev
```

The script builds the Rust generators and GPUI renderer, refreshes the ASR
catalogue, computes EQs and scores, then generates metadata, graph pictures,
and HTML before deployment. A failed step stops the update.

To rebuild one headphone locally with the existing catalogue:

```{.shell}
./update_headphones.sh --headphone "Brand Model" --force --skip-catalogue-refresh --skip-deploy
```

Use `--skip-build` to reuse compiled binaries and `--skip-check-html` to skip
the Docker-based HTML validator. `--jobs N` controls EQ and graph workers.
Use `./update_headphones.sh --help` for all options.

## Build the documentation

Install Quarto separately, then render the manual:

```{.shell}
quarto render manual
```

The rendered site is written to `dist/docs`. Code examples in the manual are
currently illustrative: execution is disabled in `manual/_quarto.yml`, so
they are not run automatically during rendering.

## Docker

The repository also contains `Dockerfile.base` and `Dockerfile` for a
containerized build:

```{.shell}
docker build -f Dockerfile.base -t spin-base:latest .
docker build -f Dockerfile -t spinorama:latest .
docker run --rm -it spinorama:latest
```

For an interactive shell with the checkout mounted:

```{.shell}
docker run --rm -it -p 5173:5173 -v "$PWD":/work spinorama:latest bash
```

Inside the container, `pytest -q tests` runs Python tests and
`npx vite --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5173` starts the website development server.
